text.p: The French government favours an alliance between state-controlled nuclear engineering group Framatome and engineering company Alcatel Alsthom, Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Friday in an interview with French afternoon daily Le Monde.
He said that General Electric Company could join the group later.
"The government is favourable to an eventual alliance between Framatome and Alcatel Alsthom in its energy activities, with GEC joining up afterward," he told the newspaper.
His comments came after Framtome said on Monday a planned merger with GEC-Alsthom seemed unlikely.

Framatome said GEC had wanted to have a 50 percent stake in the new combination, equal to its current stake in the GEC Alsthom joint venture with Alcatel Alsthom. But this desire went against the government's stipulation that French interests keep a majority in the nuclear group.
Borotra said that he wanted Framatome to be privatised and part of a strong group "the faster the better".
But, he stressed, the government "would not abandon its desire to keep its control of the nuclear domain".
